text:
incident-bot: [P1] p99 tail latency breach detected for /v1/chat/stream on dedicated-pool-hotshot-3 (us-west-2). Streaming stalls observed, clients reporting partial chunks. Auto-escalation -> @alice.sre.

alice.sre: I’m paging in. seeing p95 ~ 800ms, p99 trending 5.2s, streaming sessions stalling at tail. Queue depth on pool 3 jumped to 420 (normal ~40).

bob.runtime: Confirmed. autoscaler logs show handshake/warmup lag — new workers failing handshake for ~30s. Many requests queued waiting for warmup. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T15:02:10Z warmup: slot alloc 8 -> handshake start
2026-03-15T15:02:40Z warmup: kernel init timeout
2026-03-15T15:02:41Z handshake: mismatch backend-version
2026-03-15T15:03:01Z warmup aborted
```

carla.infra: Nothing obvious at infra level (network OK, GPU hosts healthy). packing/rack CPU fine. Looks like a runtime handshake regression after last runtime patch.

dan.perf: p50/p95/p99 snapshot for the 10m window prior to alert: 120ms / 780ms / 5.2s. Streaming stalls correlate with long warmup and KV-cache misses on hotshot pool.

elena.cs: We have 2 paying customers with active requests: AcmeCorp and NimbusAI. AcmeCorp reported "stream keeps hanging" and some 503s. CS is prepping a customer message.

alice.sre: Can we triage quick mitigation: 1) route new requests off hotshot-3 to hotshot-2 (warm) 2) scale down hotshot-3 to stop triggering new warmups 3) manual warmup retry for existing slots

bob.runtime: I can add a temporary routing rule to divert 30% of traffic for that model tag to hotshot-2. Doing `ri-router set-rule --pool hotshot-3 --fallback hotshot-2 --pct 30` now.

incident-bot: actioned: routing rule applied by bob.runtime at 2026-03-15T15:05:12Z.

carla.infra: Manually draining new scheduling to hotshot-3: `rictl pool update hotshot-3 --accept-new=false`. Doing now. This should reduce warmup churn.

bob.runtime: Also kicked a manual scale to force healthy slots instead of relying on the autoscaler: `rictl scale --pool hotshot-3 --target-instances 6 --grace 0s`

alice.sre: Good. I'm going to throttle new streaming sessions per-customer to reduce queue depth: `rate-limit: model=chat-stream, customer=generic, rps=80`

dan.perf: After routing/drain + throttle, queue depth dropped to 120 within 90s. p99 dropped to ~1.1s. Streaming stalls decreased but still seeing tail spikes for a subset of sessions.

bob.runtime: Found one suspicious handshake failure path: when a slot warms from quantized-2b -> quantized-8b variant, kernel negotiation retries 3x then gives up. Reverting that recent negotiation change to force passthrough until we patch. Applying hotfix to runtime now.

frank.prod: FYI, I’m drafting a customer incident note for AcmeCorp and NimbusAI with ETA for mitigation. Will include workaround (switch region to us-east-1 or retry).

alice.sre: After hotfix, warmup success rate for aborted handshakes improved from 62% -> 96%. Autoscaler can now complete warmup in ~8s per slot instead of 30s.

dan.perf: Current metrics: p95 400ms, p99 920ms, queue depth 35. No new 5xx spikes in last 5m.

elena.cs: Sent out customer messages: AcmeCorp acknowledged and switched critical flows to us-east-1; NimbusAI accepted a temporary rate limit. Both ask for root cause update.

alice.sre: Good work. I’ll mark this as mitigated and will hand off postmortem to eng-runtime and infra. Next actions: 1) revert negotiation change permanently pending deeper test 2) add warmup health probes to avoid handshake hangs 3) run canary on dedicated pools for handshake path.

bob.runtime: I’ll own the postmortem and the code revert + tests. Timeline: patch and canary today, full rollout after validation.

alice.sre: Closing on-call page. Will create follow-up ticket and assign owners. If anyone sees a reoccur, re-open with `!incident reopen` or ping me. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident severity set to P1 -> mitigated. Paging cleared at 2026-03-15T15:10:23Z by alice.sre.
